h1: The SEO agency Dublin firms use to be found in Google and named by AI
intro: 22 Signals is an SEO agency for Dublin and Irish businesses that also handles GEO, generative engine optimisation. We get your firm ranking in Google for Irish searches and described correctly when buyers ask ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Google AI Overviews who to hire. The work covers technical fixes, local search, answer-first content and outside mentions.

sections.h: Irish search has its own quirks
p: Ireland is a small market that shares a language with two much bigger ones. That causes problems most firms never notice. A Dublin accountancy page can rank in Britain and not at home, because nothing on it says Ireland clearly. A product page can lose to a UK retailer that ships to Ireland. A US-written blog post can attract traffic from Ohio and no enquiries from Dublin.

So the first job is making your site unmistakably Irish where it needs to be: euro prices, Irish addresses and Eircodes, Dublin postal districts where relevant, Irish regulatory references, local phone formats, and hreflang where you also run UK or US versions. Google.ie then has a clear reason to show you to Irish searchers.

list: By district: searches such as 'dentist Dublin 4', 'solicitor Dublin 2' or 'gym Dublin 8' are common, so district detail on location pages matters.
By county or suburb: Swords, Tallaght, Dún Laoghaire, Blanchardstown and Sandyford all behave as separate local markets.
By regulator or credential: Law Society of Ireland, Chartered Accountants Ireland, Central Bank authorisation and professional body memberships.
By comparison: 'best', 'reviews', 'cost' and 'vs' queries, which feed both Google and AI answers.
By assistant: more business buyers now ask ChatGPT or Gemini for a shortlist before they ever open Google.

p: Generative engine optimisation is the work of being named, and named accurately, in AI answers. It builds on SEO, because assistants rely on many of the same signals: crawlable pages, clear structure and what other trusted sites say about you. The difference is emphasis. Assistants reward consistency, clear factual statements and mentions on sources they already trust.

For an Irish firm, those sources often include the Irish Times, the Business Post, the Irish Independent, Silicon Republic, sector bodies, professional directories and well-known review platforms. If your name, services and specialisms are described the same way across your site, Google Business Profile, directories and press, assistants are far more likely to repeat that description.

list: Track a fixed set of buyer questions in Google, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Google AI Overviews, so changes are measured, not guessed.
Technical SEO: indexing, speed, structured data, internal links and site errors, fixed by people who also build websites.
Local SEO for each Dublin location: Google Business Profile, categories, photos, reviews and location pages with real detail.
Answer-first service pages and guides that state the answer in the opening lines.
Consistent company details across Irish and international directories, review sites and profiles.
Outreach for mentions in Irish trade press, sector publications and lists buyers use to shortlist.
A monthly report in plain English: what moved, why, and what comes next.

sections.h: What a first audit usually finds
list: A Google Business Profile with the wrong category, an old address or no recent photos.
Company details that differ between the website, directories and the Companies Registration Office listing.
Service pages that never say who the service is for or where it is offered.
Blog posts written for a global audience that compete with each other and help no one in Ireland.
Slow mobile pages caused by oversized images and unused scripts.
No structured data telling search engines and assistants what the business is, where it operates and what it offers.
p: None of these is dramatic on its own. Together they explain why many good Irish firms are invisible to people who would hire them.

list: Law firms: Law Society rules on solicitor advertising, careful wording on personal injuries work, and directory listings that assistants read.
Clinics and dental practices: treatment pages written clearly and accurately, with nothing that promotes prescription-only medicines to the public.
Financial services: accurate authorisation details and content that respects Central Bank expectations on promotion.
Technology companies: comparison pages, documentation and integrations pages that win high-intent searches in Ireland and across Europe.
Property: Daft.ie and MyHome.ie profiles alongside area pages for each scheme or branch.
Hospitality and retail: Google Business Profile, menus or product feeds, and reviews managed week by week.

p: We begin with a 15-minute Talk about the searches and questions that bring you work. Plan is an audit of your site, profiles, citations and presence in AI answers, delivered as a written roadmap ranked by impact within 5 to 7 days. Build is the fixes, pages and profile work, in priority order with dates in writing. Grow is monthly reporting, fresh content and the outside mentions that build trust over time.

Search work is done on your site and in your search accounts, so little of it needs anyone in the room. Monthly reviews are booked at a time that suits you, with a written report on rankings, mentions in AI answers and enquiries sent ahead of the call. For a strategy session with partners or the leadership team, we are happy to come to Dublin.

We will not promise a set number of AI mentions, publish dozens of thin pages that only swap the place name, buy links or write fake reviews. Nobody controls what an assistant says. We control the signals it reads, and we report honestly, including in the months when progress is slow.

We fix what we find. Our team also builds websites, runs paid media and produces video, so technical issues are not left waiting for another supplier, and content can include visuals that earn links. A large share of our search work is monthly SEO and content for law firms, where every legal point is checked before publishing. Dublin clients get the same standard: accuracy first, then reach.

faqs.q: What does an SEO agency Dublin firms hire actually deliver?
faqs.a: Technical fixes, local search setup, new and improved pages, consistent business details across the web, outreach for mentions and a monthly report. With GEO included, you also see how often you are named in answers to a fixed set of buyer questions in AI assistants.

faqs.q: Why does my site rank in the UK but not in Ireland?
faqs.a: Usually because the site does not signal Ireland clearly. Euro prices, Irish addresses, Eircodes, local references, a Google Business Profile in Ireland, hreflang if you have UK pages, and links from Irish sites all help Google.ie match you to Irish searches.

faqs.q: Can you guarantee we will appear in ChatGPT answers?
faqs.a: No, and nobody honestly can. We track a fixed set of questions every month and improve the signals assistants rely on, such as consistent descriptions, clear pages and mentions on trusted Irish and international sources.

faqs.q: Should we have a page for every Dublin district?
faqs.a: Only where you genuinely serve that area and have something specific to say, such as a branch, local team, parking or transport details. Pages that only swap the district name rarely rank and can harm the rest of the site.

faqs.q: How long does SEO take in Ireland?
faqs.a: Technical and profile fixes show once pages are recrawled. Ranking for competitive Dublin searches, and being named in AI answers for them, takes longer. We report progress monthly from the first month.
